### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/scenarios`, touching **31** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/qa/scenarios/README.md`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**41** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8436f67a2d522e0c700c37b69b22a083a30ce4b9`.

⛔ **13** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/qa/scenarios/README.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `created_at (literal, 46 pages)`, `/api/v1/data (route, 52 pages)`
- **9** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **1** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8436f67a2d522e0c700c37b69b22a083a30ce4b9` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `548cdefae1c9c768b2b22b4ed3d7e685ab28c730` — the merge of head `88929ff3a795fc24ae6fa1b4232c3a5e90c4416c` into base `8436f67a2d522e0c700c37b69b22a083a30ce4b9`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 548cdefae1c9c768b2b22b4ed3d7e685ab28c730 && git checkout 548cdefae1c9c768b2b22b4ed3d7e685ab28c730
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 8436f67a2d522e0c700c37b69b22a083a30ce4b9 88929ff3a795fc24ae6fa1b4232c3a5e90c4416c && git checkout -B drift-repro 8436f67a2d522e0c700c37b69b22a083a30ce4b9 && git merge --no-ff 88929ff3a795fc24ae6fa1b4232c3a5e90c4416c

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8436f67a2d522e0c700c37b69b22a083a30ce4b9
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 8436f67a2d522e0c700c37b69b22a083a30ce4b9` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `88929ff3a795fc24ae6fa1b4232c3a5e90c4416c`
Local-runs: none

### ① Derived judgments

The `Clause-②: yes (widening)` line on the changeset and the PR body is true and complete against the diff. New exports, all through `./runner`:
- from `orchestrate.ts`: `restoreObjects`, `seededRows`, `restoreSeededRows`, `SeededRows`, `RowRestore`;
- from `seed.ts`: `derivedFields`, `rowDrift`, `driftText`, `RESTORE_UNCOMPARED`, `RESTORE_UNWRITTEN`, `HeldRow`, `RowDrift`;
- the optional `AppHarness.deleteRow` with `HttpApp.deleteRow` (`app.ts`), and the optional fields `OperationResult.restored` and `HalfScores.operations.restored`.

`deleteRow` is optional, so an existing harness still compiles. A restore that needs a delete on a harness without it fails and says so. The shared `seedRowBody` is an internal refactor of `seedApp`, pinned by the parity test, which checks that the seed sends the same 8 inserts and nothing after them.

The answer that moves is the one the line names: an operation after an earlier turn's write now starts from the seeded rows. The order's five design points are each settled in the PR body:
1. **What is restored.** The seeded state is read once, as the admin, right after the seed and before any question. It covers every seeded object plus every object an operation writes or its outcome reads. Before each operation the rows are compared by id, excluding the clock, the last writer and the computed fields (`COMPUTED_VALUE_TYPES` read from the built artifact). Moved rows are restored through the seed path, as the admin, in up to three rounds: added rows deleted, removed rows reinserted with the seed's own body, changed columns set back. This is a superset of the order's object set, and the PR states why and what it costs.
2. **When.** The check, not the position, decides. A run with no drift writes nothing and is byte-identical; this is pinned.
3. **A failed restore** marks the operation NOT MEASURED with `restore: …` naming what still differs and the refusals. The operation is never asked and is counted in neither passed nor total (`opsTally` filters `notMeasured`).
4. **Interplay.** The restore runs at the head of the loop, before the first turn and never between #34293's ask and its confirmation (pinned). Questions all run before any operation at every `--ask-repeats` ask. Ask mode uses the same Run half. In a replay, an operation that leaned on an earlier write reads not measured, never a fail.
5. **Measured on eval#1's 138 records.** 628 of 1,290 operations ran after an earlier write; 199 of those failed, 198 on turn-behaviour checks and 1 on a row-state check (`send_invoice` after `add_line`'s stored probe). The PR states that an exact count needs a replay, which was not run. That is an acceptable answer to "if the records allow it".

`test/export/fixture.ts` gains `deleteRow` for its `FakeApp`. It is a test file and `src/export/**` source is untouched; accepted. The ablation is stated: removing the restore reds the cascade, confirmation-interplay and refused-restore pins.

### ② Semver level

Patch, as the changeset bumps it. `Metadata-protocol: none` holds: no spec key, card JSON or app metadata changes. The widening is new exports and optional fields of the evaluation package `@objectstack/scenarios`. `COMPUTED_VALUE_TYPES` comes from the existing `@objectstack/spec` workspace dependency, and `package.json` is unchanged. No existing export is removed or narrowed.

### ③ Boundary flags

None:
- No change under `packages/spec/src/**`, no governed path, and no platform runtime or security behaviour. The new `DELETE /api/v1/data/:object/:id` call is a runner-side client of an existing REST route, made as the admin against the scratch app.
- `src/score/**`, `src/schema.ts`, card JSONs and `src/export/**` source are untouched.
- The grader reading in the acceptance note (an extra removal on the same object is not charged to that turn) is pre-existing `src/score/**` behaviour. It is noted, not changed.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-1jp8bn`
Reviewed-by: `session_01L9qiby1cctpVpRbJzjccvY`

**VERDICT: PASS**

**失败的 job（日志抽取，best effort）：**

- **[Dogfood Regression Gate (1/3)](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/43829693775/job/133172023662)** — 失败步骤: Boot example apps and exercise real user flows

  ```
  @objectstack/dogfood:test:  FAIL   isolated  test/field-unique-rest-refusal.dogfood.test.ts > records-forms.field-unique-enforcement — the unique refusal at the REST doors > acceptance[0], negative[0]
    ↳ 失败原因: @objectstack/dogfood:test: AssertionError: expected { …(6) } to deeply equal { …(5) }
  ```

> `↳ 失败原因` 是判读的关键：**超时**（`Test timed out in …` / `Hook timed out in …`）多半是负载/时序，不是本 PR 的回归；
> **断言**（`AssertionError: …`）才指向真实的行为改变。两者的 `FAIL` 行长得一模一样，只有这一行能区分。
>
> ⚠️ **断言这一侧有一类例外，判据是断言在测什么，不是它是不是 `AssertionError`。** 断言的对象是**产品行为**（一个值、一个形状、一次拒收）⇒ 照上面读：真实的行为改变，去查，⛔ 不要重排掉；
> 断言的对象是**这次实验自身的有效性前提**（跑完的耗时、负载下的先后、任何只在时间预算内才成立的条件）⇒ 它跟**超时**是同一类，同样对负载敏感，重排一次是合法的判别手段。
> 识别是机械的：断言的消息或它比较的值本身点名了一段**时长、一个时间戳、一个耗时计数**。实测过的一对 —— `AssertionError: SecurityPlugin.init() ran: expected false to be true` 测的是产品行为（真回归）；
> `AssertionError: this run took over a second, so second-precision stamps could have differed too: expected 1006 to be less than 1000` 测的是实验前提：它守护的那条不变式当时是绿的，同一个 head 原样重排一次即成功。
> 穿着 `AssertionError` 外衣的时间测量，仍然是时间测量。（⛔ 这只改「怎么读一次红」，不改「哪些测试可以重排」——后者由别处管。）
